reasons: All three operations are directionally correct and reach the playbook's preferred position: the grant in § 2(a) now extends to Client's affiliates and to contractors acting on its behalf, § 13(b)'s licence cut-off is limited to material breach uncured after 30 days' notice (removing the near-discretionary 'any violations or breach' trigger), and § 15 now permits transfer to a successor in an M&A or substantially-all-assets transaction.

Edits are surgical: each inserts or replaces only the operative words needed (grant recipients, materiality/cure qualifier, successor carve-out) and leaves surrounding commercial terms intact. The failed minimal-edit heuristic on p0078 is an artefact of measuring the changed span; substantively only clause (b) of a long paragraph was touched, which the rule requires.

Comment is accurate, in the required voice and prefix, explains the three changes and their rationale in one sentence, and correctly offers the fallback (affiliate coverage on written notice) without lecturing.

Deviation status is properly supported: the original grant ran to Client alone, revocation of Sections 2 and 3 had no materiality or cure threshold, and § 15 covered only affiliate assignments — no successor transfer.

Minor, non-blocking drafting nit: after adding multiple licensees, 'in the ordinary course of its business' in § 2(a) is slightly ambiguous as to whose business; counterparty could be asked to conform it to 'their respective businesses'.
